text.p: Spanish government bonds ended lower, dragged down by sister European markets hit by the left's unexpected victory in the first round of the French election.
"The market has been conditioned by the French election and the tendency will be weak throughout the week," a dealer said.
The surprise at the first-round result will prompt caution and volatility before the second and final vote on June 1.
Still, the effect of the election was muted by holidays in the United Kingdom and in the United States, dealers said.

"The market has been headed down, but volume has been lower than normal. Until we see tomorrow's London open, we won't know the authentic impact of thhe French election on all European bonds," a dealer said.
Nonetheless, the Spanish market continues to be well underpinned by domestic fundamentals, dealers said.
